models_evaluated: multimodal LLM (2025 version, unnamed) via official API

links.outcome: LLM fracture detection accuracy against specialist reference in consecutive ED patients at a single center
links.effect: Concordance 808/1136 (71.1%; κ=0.634); sensitivity 76.9%, specificity 66.8%; 184 false negatives (16.2% of cohort), mostly non-displaced fractures (82.6%).
links.quote: Overall, the LLM showed good diagnostic agreement with orthopedic specialists, with concordant results in 808 of 1136 patients (71.1%; κ = 0.634; 95% CI: 68.4-73.7).

links.outcome: Missed fractures by LLM, indicating risk of standalone use as diagnosis
links.effect: False negatives were 184 patients (16.2% of cohort), 32.4% of LLM-negative assessments; 17.4% of FN cases required surgery; ankle and foot FN rates 30.4% and 17.4%.
links.quote: However, its limited ability to detect non-displaced fractures-especially in anatomically complex regions like the ankle and foot-carries direct patient safety implications and confirms that specialist review remains indispensable.

links.outcome: Fractures missed by AI negative assessments, showing risk if clinicians skip review of AI-negative cases
links.effect: 184 false-negative cases (16.2% of cohort; 32.4% of LLM-negative assessments); 82.6% non-displaced, 17.4% needed surgical treatment.
links.quote: False-negative cases accounted for 184 patients (16.2% of the total cohort), representing 32.4% of all LLM-negative assessments.

screen.reason: This is a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluating a general-purpose multimodal LLM on emergency radiographs without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
